text:
Marta: quick RFC follow-up — query layer right-sizing + RBAC delegation. TL;DR: propose splitting the console query path into a thin <router> that handles auth, lightweight projections, and fanout decisions, and a separate <executor> for expensive joins/aggregation and long-tail queries. Need quick opinions on safety, perf tradeoffs, and a migration plan.

Ajay: how thin is "thin"? are we talking only ACL checks + projection filtering, or also short-circuit aggregations for single-tenant views?

Marta: aim is ACL + projection + cheap prefetches (single-row lookups, cached small materializations). Anything that touches large aggregates or cross-tenant joins goes to executor. Goal: reduce token/CPU cost in router and let router remain scale-friendly under burst.

Sanjeev: telemetry question — if we split, we need distinct SLOs and error signals for router vs executor. router must have 99.95 latency SLO for 95th (sub-100ms target). executor SLO can be more lenient but must expose queue depth and tail latency histograms.

Hao: interface thought: gRPC streaming between router and executor to let router push partial filters / KV cache hints and accept a streaming result set. Example contract sketch:
```
rpc Execute(QueryRequest) returns (stream QueryRow);
message QueryRequest { string view = 1; map<string,string> filters = 2; repeated string hints = 3; }
```
Pro: backpressure and partial answers. Con: more operational complexity than HTTP+json. Thoughts?

Lexi: migration/playbook idea — start with opt-in routes: mark a small percentage of dashboard routes to go through router-only mode (router answers from cache/materializations) and compare correctness/perf. Then gradually flip heavy queries to executor by route tag. Need feature-flag + per-route telemetry.

Marta: agree re feature flags. Also need RBAC semantics: two options we discussed earlier — (A) pushdown: router evaluates ACL and sends an allowed-filter token to executor; executor trusts token and skips ACL checks (faster), or (B) double-check: executor repeats ACL check (slower but safer). Which do we prefer?

Ajay: I prefer (A) but only if router token is cryptographically signed and short-lived + includes trace id and route fingerprint. Otherwise (B) for initial rollout.

Sanjeev: +1 to signed tokens. Also we should track metrics: acl_verifications.router, acl_verifications.executor, token_reject_rate, token_age_secs. We want to be able to audit if executor ever received a request without valid token.

Hao: on data plane isolation — executor should run in a different pool (dedicated nodes) so noisy aggregations don't starve router. Also consider CPU pinning and niceness for router.

Lexi: canary plan sketch: 1) prove correctness in staging; 2) deploy router-only for cached dashboards in prod behind FF; 3) enable signed-token pushdown for canary routes with executor double-check enabled; 4) disable double-check after 2 weeks of zero rejects and stable metrics; 5) ramp executor-only for heavy routes.

Marta: timeline suggestion: 3 weeks of prototyping (router+signed token), 2 weeks staging bake, 4 weeks staged rollouts. Will create a short RFC update with a migration checklist.

Ajay: one more perf tradeoff — router doing too many projections increases memory bandwidth and can hurt tail for small requests. Add a knob to limit router per-request CPU/time, fallback to executor when exceeded. E.g. router_budget_ms = 30ms.

Marta: good call. We should expose that as a per-route config and a global safe default.

deploy-bot: Marta triggered deploy: "query-router-experiment:v0.1" -> staging at 2024-11-04T18:07:12Z :building_worker:

Hao: thanks — I'll prototype gRPC contract and a small harness for signed tokens. I'll post API proto and minimal test harness soon.

Lexi: I'll draft the migration checklist and telemetry dashboards (SLO, error budget burn, token rejects, route-level p95/p99).

Marta: awesome. If anyone has objections to the signed-token pushdown approach, speak now; otherwise I'll update the RFC and attach a proposed rollout playbook. :thumbsup:
